TrashTalk, c'est la référence du paysage: TrashTalk is the reference of the French-language NBA scene. Started in 2014 as a specialist article site, the outlet quickly moved into video with its YouTube channel — and today it's a complete ecosystem: audio podcast, YouTube, Twitch, X for real-time news, and even books on basketball culture since 2018.
Au cœur du projet, deux co-fondateurs :: At the heart of the project are two co-founders: Bastien Fontanieu (aka BSL), the emotional engine, a journalist formerly at L'Équipe who found traditional editorial rules too restrictive and built his own stage — and Alexandre Martin, the perfect partner, calmer, more analytical, the one who puts the stats back on the table when the discussion gets too emotional. The volcanic enthusiast and the measured analyst: when the chemistry is there, the audience feels it immediately.
Le nom n'est pas choisi au hasard : le t: The name isn't random: trash talk, in NBA culture, is the art of provoking your opponent. Serious analysis — stats, context, stakes — but always with irony, tongue-in-cheek humour and plenty of banter. Accessible, but never superficial.
Les Apéros TrashTalk (discussion libre s: The TrashTalk Apéros (free discussion on a hot topic), the Top 10 per franchise and all-time Top 100 (built, argued, debated content that lasts), and the Week Pass (weekly NBA recap). Hot news + long-term depth: it creates a regular date and builds loyalty.
Des centaines de milliers de fans sur X,: Hundreds of thousands of fans on X, live-tweets during games, the Draft… and viewing parties at the Grand Rex — Europe's biggest cinema, 2,700 seats, packed to watch NBA games live at 2 a.m. Marketing genius or a well-organised cult? Probably both. But a cult with very good defensive analysis.
Les limites ? Certains reprochent un ton: The limits? Some find the tone too "passionate debate", not analytical enough — this isn't Thinking Basketball — and the digital experience (the app) could be smoother. But what stands out everywhere: consistency, passion, and a fully owned editorial line. That's what makes the whole thing coherent.
Pour Jael, notre invité, l'impact est ré: For Jael, our guest, the impact is real: coming from football, it was TrashTalk that gave him his basketball culture over the last 7-8 years. And beyond the outlet itself, TrashTalk is a strong French-language voice in a world dominated by American media — NBA culture in French, accessible, speaking as much to long-time fans as to newcomers. Rare and precious.
« TrashTalk n'a pas juste créé une audie: “TrashTalk didn't just build an audience. They built a tribe — 2,700 people at the Grand Rex at 2 a.m. to watch basketball. It's no longer an outlet, it's a rallying point.” — Lolo & Jael
